title: City subgrants following findings on the same federal program
question: Which federal programs appear in a subrecipient audit and a later City-reported subaward?
finding: 3 program-and-finding combinations at 2 recipients meet the screen. PRC’s later audit records its 2022 payroll finding as resolved.
how: Join audited City-paid organizations to Treasury by identical Unique Entity ID and federal assistance listing. Require the underlying audited award to name the City as pass-through and a positive subgrant action after the audit was accepted. Restrict the Treasury comparison to prime records listing one program. Group by report, finding and program.
limits: Findings concern the earlier audit period. They do not establish that later awards had unsupported costs. The audit subset covers organizations identified in the City-paid organization comparison, and program records can contain multiple contracts. No dollars are summed across subaward rows. For the fiscal years covered here, the federal audit threshold depends on the start of the entity’s fiscal year. It was $750,000 in federal awards expended across all programs for years starting before October 1, 2024, and $1 million for years starting on or after that date. An entity reaches the threshold at either amount. City payments alone cannot establish how much federal funding the recipient expended.

sources.t: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, downloadable audit datasets
PRC FY2023 audit, prior findings, p. 31
Federal Audit Clearinghouse, expenditure thresholds by fiscal-year start date
